record.paper_title: Open Questions on Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Chemical Reaction Networks
record.original_question: How can a thermodynamic theory be developed for chemical reaction networks with mixed dynamics, where some low-copy-number species must be treated stochastically while much more abundant species can be treated deterministically, so that cellular switching mechanisms can be analyzed for reliability and energetic cost?

evidence.quote: Biochemical complexity emerges at the subcellular level in part because some species with very low molecular number coexists with others with many orders of magnitude more molecules. The former provide the versatility (via fluctuations) while the latter the stability (via deterministic attractors) necessary for a cell to reliably switch between different modes of operation. To be able to analyze such mechanisms and assess their reliability and energetic cost, a thermodynamics for CRNs described by mixed dynamics (i.e. dynamics which can treat some species stochastically and other deterministically) needs to be developed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a chemical reaction network (CRN) consisting of a finite set of chemical species $\{X_i\}$ undergoing a finite set of elementary reactions $\rho: \sum_i \nu_{i\rho}^- X_i \rightleftharpoons \sum_i \nu_{i\rho}^+ X_i$ with mass-action kinetics, in a well-mixed reactor of volume $V$ in contact with chemostats and a heat bath at inverse temperature $\beta$. Partition the species into two disjoint classes:

(i) a "low-copy-number" class $L$ whose molecular counts $n_i$ ($i \in L$) remain of order $1$ and whose dynamics must be modeled by a continuous-time Markov jump process (chemical master equation) with reaction propensities derived from stochastic mass-action;

(ii) a "high-copy-number" class $H$ whose concentrations $c_j = N_j/V$ ($j \in H$) are well approximated, in the relevant limit, by deterministic chemical rate equations $\dot c_j = \sum_\rho (\nu_{j\rho}^+ - \nu_{j\rho}^-)\, k_\rho \prod_i c_i^{\nu_{i\rho}^-}$.

Develop a self-consistent nonequilibrium thermodynamic theory for such CRNs with mixed stochastic-deterministic ("hybrid") dynamics. Specifically:

1. Define and justify, from a partial thermodynamic / macroscopic limit on the species in $H$ while retaining stochasticity for species in $L$, dynamical equations that couple the master equation for $\{n_i\}_{i\in L}$ to the rate equations for $\{c_j\}_{j\in H}$, in a way that respects local detailed balance with respect to the chemical potentials $\mu_i = \mu_i^\circ + \beta^{-1} \ln c_i$ of all species.

2. Derive the corresponding first and second laws, identifying the system entropy, the heat exchanged with the bath, the chemical work performed by chemostats, and a non-negative entropy production rate $\dot\Sigma \ge 0$ decomposed into a stochastic (discrete-reaction) contribution and a deterministic (continuous-reaction) contribution.

3. Apply the resulting framework to cellular switching motifs in which low-abundance regulatory species (treated stochastically) modulate the deterministic dynamics of abundant species, and quantify the trade-offs between switching reliability (e.g.\ mean first-passage times between attractors, error rates) and the thermodynamic cost (entropy production, dissipated free energy).
artifact.category_tag: Stochastic thermodynamics of chemical reaction networks
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 work ("What is a chemostat? Insights from hybrid dynamics and stochastic thermodynamics", arXiv:2502.17257) develops a thermodynamically consistent framework for hybrid CRNs in which low-abundance species evolve stochastically while high-abundance species evolve deterministically, deriving local detailed balance and a decomposition of the entropy production into stochastic and deterministic parts via a partial macroscopic limit. This addresses the foundational thermodynamic framework, but the broader program—particularly systematic application to cellular switching reliability/cost trade-offs—is only partially completed.

status_evidence.title: What is a chemostat? Insights from hybrid dynamics and stochastic thermodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes thermodynamic consistency for hybrid CRNs partitioning species into low-abundance (stochastic) and high-abundance (deterministic) classes, derives local detailed balance and entropy production decomposition via a partial macroscopic limit.
status_evidence.claim: A hybrid stochastic-deterministic thermodynamic framework for CRNs has been formulated.

status_evidence.title: Information Thermodynamics for Deterministic Chemical Reaction Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Extends nonequilibrium thermodynamics of CRNs in the deterministic regime, complementary to stochastic treatments.
status_evidence.claim: Deterministic-side thermodynamic theory continues to be refined alongside stochastic CRN thermodynamics.
